name: FL-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+20 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Wasserman Schultz holds a massive fundraising advantage ($1.9M cash vs $41K)
Republican challenger is underfunded and little known
model.rationale: The D+20 district fundamentals, the incumbent's overwhelming financial edge, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win near 94% all point the same way. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, this stays safely Democratic.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the Republican within single digits, or a major scandal involving the incumbent, would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D) is running.

overview:
Debbie Wasserman Schultz defends a South Florida seat with a strong Democratic lean after Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick's resignation. She enters the general election as a well-known incumbent with roughly $1.9 million on hand, dwarfing Republican Brent Andersen's modest war chest of about $41,000. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged, and independent Kedner Maxime raises little.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give Democrats about a 94% chance of holding the seat. The combination of a D+20 lean, incumbency, and a lopsided resource gap makes this a Safe Democratic race, with only modest residual uncertainty from the absence of polling.
